steps: Assess organ involvement and severity (esp. renal, CNS, haematological).
Moderate–severe / organ-threatening: high-dose corticosteroids + immunosuppression (mycophenolate/cyclophosphamide; biologics).
Hydroxychloroquine for essentially all patients (reduces flares).
Exclude/treat concurrent infection (mimics flare and complicates immunosuppression); sun protection, vaccination.

drugRefs.dose: 200–400 mg PO once daily (≤5 mg/kg actual body weight/day)
drugRefs.why: Recommended for essentially all SLE patients — reduces flares, organ damage and mortality; baseline/annual retinal screening required.

drugRefs.dose: low dose (≤7.5 mg/day) for mild; up to 0.5 mg/kg/day short course for moderate, then taper
drugRefs.why: Controls active inflammation; use the lowest effective dose and taper to minimise long-term steroid toxicity.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
2019 EULAR Recommendations for the Management of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
2019 EULAR/ERA-EDTA Recommendations for the Management of Lupus Nephritis

recommendations.regimenLabel: Organ-threatening / severe flare — pulse steroids + immunosuppression

drugRefs.why: Rapid control of severe/organ-threatening flares (e.g. nephritis, CNS, severe cytopenias) before/with maintenance immunosuppression.
First-line induction/maintenance for lupus nephritis and other severe manifestations; teratogenic — ensure contraception.

drugRefs.dose: 500 mg IV every 2 weeks for 6 doses (Euro-Lupus low-dose regimen)
drugRefs.why: Induction option for severe lupus nephritis or life-threatening disease; requires fertility counselling and bladder protection.

decision.label: Exclude infection; escalate immunosuppression by severity

confirm: Multisystem flare (rash, arthritis, serositis, cytopenias, nephritis) in known/new SLE; raised anti-dsDNA, low complement.
